title: Factorization through a regular surface point blowdown
statement: Let $T$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth], regular of dimension two [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $x\in T$ be a reduced closed point and let $b:W=\operatorname{Bl}_xT\to T$ be its blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup], with exceptional fibre $E=b^{-1}(x)$. For any scheme $Z$ [def-pc-scheme] and morphism $f:W\to Z$ whose topological image $f(E)$ is one point, there is a unique morphism $g:T\to Z$ such that $f=gb$.

source.place: Tag 0C5J (lemma-factor-through-contraction), applied to the exceptional curve of a regular surface point blowup.

proof.text: Write $f(E)=\{z\}$. In particular $E\ne\varnothing$. The blowup is an isomorphism over $T\setminus\{x\}$ by [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement]. Hence $b$ is surjective, with singleton fibres away from $x$ and fibre $E$ over $x$. It is proper by [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper]: the ideal of the reduced closed point is quasi-coherent and locally finitely generated because $T$ is Noetherian. Properness includes universal closedness [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $b$ is a closed map. Finally [lem-sfb-regular-point-blowup-functions] gives the canonical sheaf isomorphism $\beta:\mathcal O_T\xrightarrow{\sim}b_*\mathcal O_W$, including its restriction compatibility. The auxiliary result applies also when $x$ has local dimension less than two.

Define a set map $g:T\to Z$ by $g(x)=z$ and, for $t\ne x$, $g(t)=f(w)$ for the unique $w$ above $t$. Thus $f=g\circ b$. For an open $V\subseteq Z$, put $A=g^{-1}V$. Then $b^{-1}A=f^{-1}V$ is open and surjectivity gives $T\setminus A=b(W\setminus f^{-1}V)$. The right side is closed because $b$ is closed. Thus $A$ is open and $g$ is continuous. Surjectivity also proves uniqueness of this underlying map.

For each open $V\subseteq Z$, set $U=g^{-1}V$ and define $g^\sharp_V=\beta_U^{-1}\circ f^\sharp_V:\mathcal O_Z(V)\to\mathcal O_T(U)$, using $f^{-1}V=b^{-1}U$. These are unital ring homomorphisms. For $V_1\subseteq V_2$, restriction commutes with $f^\sharp$ and with $\beta$ and hence with $\beta^{-1}$, so the displayed maps form a sheaf morphism $\mathcal O_Z\to g_*\mathcal O_T$. By the definition of composition of ringed-space morphisms, $g^\sharp$ satisfies $f^\sharp_V=\beta_{g^{-1}V}\circ g^\sharp_V$ on every $V$. Consequently $(g,g^\sharp)\circ b=f$ as morphisms of ringed spaces.

For each $t\in T$, choose $w\in W$ with $b(w)=t$, and put $y=g(t)=f(w)$. Passing the equality of ringed-space morphisms to stalks gives $f^\sharp_w=b^\sharp_w\circ g^\sharp_t$. If $a$ is in the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{Z,y}$, locality of $f^\sharp_w$ makes $f^\sharp_w(a)$ a nonunit. Were $g^\sharp_t(a)$ a unit, its image under the unital ring homomorphism $b^\sharp_w$ would be a unit, a contradiction. Thus $g^\sharp_t(a)$ is a nonunit, hence belongs to the maximal ideal of the local ring $\mathcal O_{T,t}$. Every stalk map of $g$ is local, so $g$ is a morphism of schemes.

Let $h:T\to Z$ satisfy $h\circ b=f$. Surjectivity of $b$ gives $h=g$ on points. For every open $V\subseteq Z$, composition gives $\beta_{g^{-1}V}\circ h^\sharp_V=f^\sharp_V=\beta_{g^{-1}V}\circ g^\sharp_V$. Cancel the isomorphism $\beta_{g^{-1}V}$ to obtain $h^\sharp_V=g^\sharp_V$. Equality on all opens gives $h=g$ as ringed-space morphisms and hence as scheme morphisms. This proves existence and uniqueness.
